expectations.text: An ADMIN role/value was added to the project's role model (e.g. the Role enum), rather than hardcoding a separate ad-hoc check unrelated to the existing role system.
expectations.evidence: Report: 'Role enum — added ADMIN alongside the existing USER.'

expectations.text: GET /api/admin/users is restricted so only an ADMIN-authenticated caller can access it, and a regular USER-authenticated request to it is expected to receive a 403, not a 200.
expectations.evidence: Report: added '.requestMatchers("/api/admin/**").hasRole("ADMIN")'; AdminControllerTest explicitly covers 'Cookie for a USER-role account -> 403', 'Cookie for an ADMIN-role account -> 200', both confirmed passing in the real test run.

expectations.text: The admin users endpoint returns a DTO for each user (matching the project's existing dto package convention) rather than serializing the raw User JPA entity directly.
expectations.evidence: Report: 'AdminController ... returns List<UserResponse> built by mapping UserService.getAllUsers() through the existing UserResponse.from(User) factory.'

expectations.text: The logic for listing users lives in a service class; the new controller method stays thin (delegates to the service rather than querying the repository or applying business logic itself).
expectations.evidence: Report: 'UserService.getAllUsers() — new read-only transactional method ... AdminController delegates to UserService.getAllUsers()', explicitly 'to keep the Controller -> Service -> Repository layering intact rather than having the controller call the repository directly.'

expectations.text: Before writing code, the agent explained what it was about to implement and which files it would touch; after implementing, it ran the Maven test suite (or at least a compile) and reported the real outcome rather than an unverified claim of success.
